evidence.note: Systematic environment probing before building: OS, python/node/go/rust availability, pip/npm, internet reachability to pypi, pre-installed packages (playwright), data dir — chose aiohttp stack from real constraints.
Caught explicit/subtle contract requirements: emoji-picker grid instead of prompt(), password_hash must be stripped from responses, computed reply_count — real spec-reading, not blind CRUD.
Re-read spec and caught the subtle 'data-testid selectors present in served HTML' requirement (not just JS-rendered), rewriting index.html with a static skeleton — genuine sharp-edge extraction.

Tracked contract families (44 testids, 28 API assertions, member usernames, GET invitations missing) but treated seq density anomaly ('1 then 3 due to events table') casually rather than investigating the dense-per-channel invariant.
IRC JOIN/numerics/dense-seq-across-writers left broken and consciously deferred; role gating, mention exclusion, resume.gap never surfaced or verified — many named subtle traps unaddressed.

reasoning: Environment probing was thorough and decision-driving (anchor-8 quality), and the agent extracted main per-subsystem contracts plus several genuine sharp edges (testid-in-served-HTML, emoji-picker vs prompt, password_hash, computed reply_count). But it never built a systematic/referenced contract inventory, and left many named subtle traps (role gating, mention exclusion, transfer_ownership, resume.gap, dense-seq-across-writers) unsurfaced or unverified — so it lands above the '5' (main contracts + runtime) but short of the systematic trap-surfacing at '8'.
